title: ARDS — refractory hypoxemia on the vent
summary: 52M with influenza A pneumonia intubated 2 h ago in the ED on non-protective settings; severe hypoxemia on arrival to the MICU.
objectives: Calculate predicted body weight and set VT ~6 mL/kg PBW
Measure plateau pressure; target Pplat ≤30 and driving pressure ≤15 cmH2O
Apply a PEEP/FiO2 strategy and accept permissive hypercapnia
Prone ≥16 h/day when P/F <150 on FiO2 ≥0.6 and PEEP ≥5; consider early neuromuscular blockade

problems: Influenza A pneumonia (rapid test positive in ED)
chart.hpi: 5 days of fever, myalgias and cough, 2 days of progressive dyspnea. In the ED SpO2 78% on non-rebreather; intubated with etomidate/rocuronium and placed on VC 550 mL, RR 18, PEEP 5, FiO2 0.8. Transferred to MICU 2 h after intubation.
chart.pmh: Hypertension. Obesity. No known lung disease. Unvaccinated for influenza this season.
meds: Oseltamivir 75 mg (first dose given in ED)
chart.social: Bus driver. Never smoker. Lives with wife.
chart.exam: Sedated, RASS −3. Diffuse coarse crackles bilaterally. Equal breath sounds. Warm extremities, CRT 3 s. No edema.

stages.name: Arrival — hypoxemic on initial settings
stages.nurse: Sat is 86 on 80 percent. The ED settings haven't been touched.
stages.cue: VT 550 = 8.3 mL/kg PBW; Pplat ~36, DP ~31. Expect: PBW calculation, VT ~400, PEEP 12–14, RR up to 28–30, plateau check, repeat ABG.

branches.label: Lung-protective settings: VT ~400, PEEP 12–14, RR up

stages.name: Lung-protective settings
stages.nurse: Sat is up to 90. Gas is back — pH 7.24. Do you want bicarb?
stages.cue: Pplat ~31, DP ~17, P/F ~83 → severe ARDS. pH 7.24 is acceptable (permissive hypercapnia; no bicarb). Next: prone + NMB; consider recruitment/PEEP titration.

branches.label: Raises tidal volume to correct CO2 / gives bicarbonate

stages.name: Proned + paralyzed
stages.nurse: He's prone. Sat 95 — can we come down on the oxygen?
stages.cue: Success. Discuss ≥16 h prone sessions, FiO2 wean target SpO2 88–95%, conservative fluids once off pressors, ECMO criteria if worsening.

stages.name: Refractory hypoxemia
stages.nurse: Sat's 79 and dropping. What do you want to do?
stages.cue: Exclude tube/plug/PTX (DOPES), then lung-protective settings and prone. Discuss ECMO referral (P/F <80 >6 h, pH <7.25 with PaCO2 ≥60).

a.text: Inspiratory hold: Pplat 36 cmH2O, PEEP 5 → driving pressure 31. Ppeak 41.

b.text: Inspiratory hold: Pplat 31 cmH2O, PEEP 14 → driving pressure 17. Ppeak 36.

c.text: Inspiratory hold: Pplat 28 cmH2O, PEEP 14 → driving pressure 14.

d.text: Inspiratory hold: Pplat 36 cmH2O, PEEP 5 → driving pressure 31.

autopeep.text: Expiratory hold: total PEEP equals set PEEP (no intrinsic PEEP).

cxr.text: Portable AP: ETT tip 4 cm above the carina. Diffuse bilateral airspace opacities. No pneumothorax. No large effusion. Cardiac silhouette normal size. OG tube in stomach.

lus.text: Bilateral lung sliding present. Diffuse bilateral B-lines with irregular pleural line and subpleural consolidations, worst at the bases. No effusion. No pneumothorax.

echo_pocus.text: Hyperdynamic LV, EF >60%. RV mildly dilated (RV:LV ~0.8), normal function, no septal flattening. No pericardial effusion. IVC 2.1 cm, minimal respiratory variation.

tte.text: LVEF 65%. RV mildly dilated with normal systolic function (TAPSE 19 mm). Estimated RVSP 38 mmHg. No significant valvular disease.

rvp.text: Influenza A (H1N1) DETECTED. RSV, SARS-CoV-2 and other targets not detected.

sputum.text: Gram stain: many PMNs, no predominant organism. Culture pending.

ecg.text: Sinus tachycardia 112. Normal axis. No acute ST changes.

ct_chest.text: Bilateral dependent consolidation with ground-glass opacities, gradient anterior to posterior. No pneumothorax. (Note: patient transported on FiO2 1.0; desaturated to 82% during transfer.)

prone.text: Proned with 5-person team; ETT and lines secured. Instructor will report the response.

cisatra.text: Cisatracurium bolus and infusion started; sedation deepened to RASS −5 first.

teaching: PBW (male) = 50 + 0.91 × (height cm − 152.4); 170 cm → 66 kg, so 6 mL/kg ≈ 400 mL.
Driving pressure (Pplat − PEEP) tracks mortality in ARDS; target ≤15 cmH2O.
PROSEVA: prone ≥16 h/day for P/F <150 reduced 28-day mortality.
Permissive hypercapnia: pH ≥7.20–7.25 is acceptable; bicarbonate does not fix the problem.
Transporting a P/F <100 patient to CT is a risk with little benefit when the bedside answer is already clear.
